findings.claim: The #if guard `!NETSTANDARD2_0 && !NETFRAMEWORK` omits the attribute on netstandard2.0/.NET Framework builds, which contradicts the requirement that ALL generated code carry ExcludeFromCodeCoverage. ExcludeFromCodeCoverageAttribute has existed since .NET Framework 4.0 and netstandard2.0, so the guard looks unnecessary. Users targeting those frameworks, including Unity-style consumers, still get coverage skew.

findings.claim: CompositeResolverTemplate emits the attribute unconditionally, bypassing the new Options.Generator.ExcludeFromCodeCoverage opt-out used in every other template. A user who sets ExcludeFromCodeCoverage=false still gets the attribute on composite resolvers, and the generated output is inconsistent.

receipt_plan.detail: Generate a composite resolver with [GeneratedMessagePackResolver(ExcludeFromCodeCoverage=false)] semantics and assert the output does not contain ExcludeFromCodeCoverage. It currently does.

findings.claim: The change to the nesting emitter, `{` to `{\r\n`, alters the whitespace of generated output for nested types with constraints. This may break users' checked-in or snapshot generator output and is unrelated to the requirement. It is a compatibility-visible output change.

The analyzer reads the property by name via GetSingleNamedArgumentValue. An older MessagePack runtime paired with a newer generator is compatible, but a newer runtime with an older analyzer silently ignores the property.
